protections: On a redirect whose host or scheme changes, the outgoing request must not carry the Authorization header (defaultScrubSensitiveHeaders at packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:67-93, invoked from packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/redirectHandler.ts:133-136).

On a redirect whose host or scheme changes, the outgoing request must not carry the Cookie header (same guard, packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:81) - the two headers are one guard and therefore one protection.

packages/http/fetch/src/fetchRequestAdapter.ts:441-446 authenticates, then sends that lowercased map through httpClient.executeFetch
packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/redirectHandler.ts:133-136 hands fetchRequestInit.headers to currentOptions.scrubSensitiveHeaders
packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:79-82 deletes only the exact-case properties headers.Authorization and headers.Cookie, so 'authorization'/'cookie' survive
packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:77 shows the host/protocol comparison itself is already case-insensitive, so the defect is only the header-name match

packages/abstractions/src/authentication/baseBearerTokenAuthenticationProvider.ts:14,34 stores the token under 'Authorization' inside a case-insensitive Headers record and packages/abstractions/src/recordWithCaseInsensitiveKeys.ts:84-86 returns the original spelling on ownKeys, which :531 then lowercases

packages/http/fetch/test/node/RedirectHandlerOptions.ts:63-73 and test/node/RedirectHandler.ts:329-353 build canonical-case header objects by hand, so the shipped tests never exercise the adapter-produced lowercase map

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The second writer only runs when a BaseBearerTokenAuthenticationProvider is passed to KiotaClientFactory (kiotaClientFactory.ts:52-54) and the adapter has already authenticated, so the write looks redundant rather than a security path; the handler and headersUtil are plain-object helpers with no casing contract.
evidence: packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/authorizationHandler.ts:53 and :67 set the header under the canonical spelling 'Authorization' (constant at :23) on a map whose other keys were lowercased at fetchRequestAdapter.ts:531

packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/authorizationHandler.ts:80 looks the token up with the same canonical spelling, so it never sees the adapter's 'authorization' key and writes a second spelling of the same header
packages/http/fetch/src/utils/headersUtil.ts:20-24 and :33-39 index the plain object by the exact key string, so no spelling agreement is enforced anywhere
packages/http/fetch/src/kiotaClientFactory.ts:50-54 shows this handler is part of a supported public configuration (third parameter authenticationProvider)

consequence at the guard: a fix that deletes only the lowercased keys ('authorization'/'cookie') leaves this canonical 'Authorization' in place, and a fix that keeps the current canonical delete leaves the adapter's key in place - one spelling survives either half-fix
packages/http/fetch/test/common/middleware/authorizationHandler.ts:22-33 also uses canonical-case header objects, so nothing pins the mixed-spelling case

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The scrub's own comments state that Proxy-Authorization is not applicable to the Fetch API because proxy configuration is handled below JavaScript (redirectHandlerOptions.ts:61-62 and :89-92).
evidence: packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:79-82 names only Authorization and Cookie; no Proxy-Authorization, X-Api-Key or other caller-supplied credential name is removed
packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:60-62 and :89-92 argue the omission away in comments

packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:67-93 is private static and not exported, so callers cannot extend the roster without replacing scrubSensitiveHeaders wholesale via the constructor option at :133

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The repository documents the omission as intentional ('Browser environment doesn't require a RedirectHandler middleware', packages/http/fetch/docs/design/isomorphic.md:39) because browsers follow redirects themselves, so this chain never had to scrub.
evidence: packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/browser/middlewareFactory.ts:29-30 returns [RetryHandler, ParametersNameDecodingHandler, UserAgentHandler, HeadersInspectionHandler, UrlReplaceHandler, CustomFetchHandler] - no RedirectHandler and no equivalent scrub
packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/middlewareFactory.ts:30 shows the node chain does insert new RedirectHandler() second, so the parallel browser copy diverged

packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/redirectHandler.ts:175 shows why the node handler cannot simply be dropped into the browser chain: it forces redirect='manual'

traps.reason_to_dismiss: convertToNativeRequest is the documented hand-off for callers that execute the request themselves (packages/abstractions/src/requestAdapter.ts:96-100), so redirect policy looks like the caller's responsibility.
evidence: packages/http/fetch/src/fetchRequestAdapter.ts:556-565 authenticates at :560 and returns the same RequestInit built at :529-537, but never wraps it in a middleware chain and never sets a redirect policy
packages/http/fetch/src/fetchRequestAdapter.ts:533-537 builds only method/headers/body, so the returned init has no 'redirect' key and the caller's fetch follows redirects by default

packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/redirectHandler.ts:175 is the only place in the package that sets redirect='manual', and it is reachable only through the middleware chain that convertToNativeRequest bypasses
packages/http/fetch/src/fetchRequestAdapter.ts:441-446 shows the sibling entry point (sendAsync) takes the chain route to the same header map

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The caller explicitly supplied the middleware list, which is the documented way to customise the pipeline (kiotaClientFactory.ts:19-47); both KiotaClientFactory.create with an empty list and the HttpClient constructor fall back to the default chain, so only an intentional non-empty custom list omits the RedirectHandler.
evidence: packages/http/fetch/src/kiotaClientFactory.ts:50-55 uses middlewares || MiddlewareFactory.getDefaultMiddlewares(customFetch), so any non-empty caller array replaces the chain and can omit RedirectHandler
packages/http/fetch/src/httpClient.ts:27 keeps a non-empty custom chain as-is (middlewares?.length && middlewares[0]) and only falls back to the default chain for an empty/undefined list
packages/http/fetch/test/node/kiotaClientFactory.ts:27-39 pins that a caller-supplied array is used verbatim and in order, so forcing a RedirectHandler in would break a tested contract

masking: Fix A (the redirect-vulnerability scrub that landed in 1.0.0-preview.100, packages/http/fetch/CHANGELOG.md:22-24) introduced the guard at redirectHandlerOptions.ts:79-82 but never matched its own input; fixing the scrub's case handling (T1) makes T4 the next carrier, because AuthorizationHandler.ts:53 writes a canonical-case token that a lowercase-only delete misses.

Fixing the producer by deleting .toLocaleLowerCase() at fetchRequestAdapter.ts:531 only helps when the source Headers record holds a canonical spelling; the case-insensitive record returns the caller's original spelling on iteration (recordWithCaseInsensitiveKeys.ts:84-86), so a caller-supplied 'AUTHORIZATION' still defeats an exact-case scrub - the producer fix masks the remaining shape rather than closing it.

Once the scrub actually deletes headers, the same-host/same-scheme and relative-redirect paths become the observable constraint (test/node/RedirectHandler.ts:259-283 and :380-405): a fix that strips on every redirect trades T1 for an authentication regression on intra-service redirects.

conflicts.what: A fix that deletes only the lowercased spelling satisfies the adapter route but leaves AuthorizationHandler's canonical 'Authorization' (authorizationHandler.ts:53); normalising every header name to lowercase at the shared headersUtil layer satisfies T4 but changes the keys every other middleware and caller sees, and still leaves the scrub's exact-case delete unmatched unless the scrub is also changed.

The obvious fix for T2 (insert the existing RedirectHandler into the browser default chain) reuses T1's scrub but also sets redirect='manual' (redirectHandler.ts:175); in a browser the resulting redirect response is opaque, has no readable Location header (redirectHandler.ts:84-96), so same-origin and cross-origin redirect following - the must-keep-working behaviour the browser chain exists for - stops working.

Copying T1's credential strip into convertToNativeRequest breaks that method's documented purpose of handing a fully authenticated native request to the caller (abstractions/src/requestAdapter.ts:96-100); the only non-breaking hardening there is a redirect policy (redirect:'manual'), a different contract from the scrub.

fairness_risks: Same-host and same-scheme redirects must keep Authorization and Cookie (packages/http/fetch/test/node/RedirectHandler.ts:380-405) and relative-URL redirects must keep them too (:259-283); an over-broad 'strip on every redirect' rule breaks authentication that currently works.

A caller-supplied scrubSensitiveHeaders must still be honoured (packages/http/fetch/test/node/RedirectHandler.ts:407-440; option wiring at packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:133); a fix that always strips ignores the documented option.

convertToNativeRequest must keep returning an authenticated request, headers and body included (packages/abstractions/src/requestAdapter.ts:96-100); stripping credentials there would make the method useless for callers that execute requests themselves.

The browser default chain must keep letting the browser follow redirects (packages/http/fetch/docs/design/isomorphic.md:39); installing a handler that forces redirect='manual' in that chain would regress every browser consumer.

A caller-supplied middleware array must stay verbatim and ordered (packages/http/fetch/test/node/kiotaClientFactory.ts:27-39); forcing a RedirectHandler into it would break the documented customisation and opt-out contract.

The alternative fix of removing the lowercasing at packages/http/fetch/src/fetchRequestAdapter.ts:531 changes the header-name contract for every consumer, including the package's own lowercase lookup at packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/retryHandler.ts:84, so it is not a free change.

design.why: T1 is the anchor the report names, so it is easy, but a correct fix must also keep same-host/same-scheme and relative redirects authenticated (test/node/RedirectHandler.ts:380-405, :259-283) and must keep honouring a caller-supplied scrubber (:407-440) - that coupled value is what punishes the obvious over-hardening. T4 forces the fix to be genuinely case-insensitive rather than deleting one spelling, because a supported configuration has AuthorizationHandler writing a canonical-case token onto the adapter's lowercased map (authorizationHandler.ts:53,:80 via kiotaClientFactory.ts:52-54); a half-fix passes T1's test and still leaks. T2 and T3 are the two deepseek-type traps: the same protection is absent on two routes with two different documented dismissals (browser chain per docs/design/isomorphic.md:39; native hand-off per abstractions/src/requestAdapter.ts:96-100) and at two different fix sites, and neither can be closed by copying T1's strip (the browser chain cannot force redirect:'manual'; the native hand-off must stay authenticated). T5 rides along inside T1's roster. T6 is excluded: forcing a RedirectHandler into a caller-supplied middleware list contradicts a tested, documented customisation contract, so it is a distractor rather than a gradable missing protection. This design beats 'just make the scrub case-insensitive' (leaves T2 and T3 untouched with no reason to have looked at them) and beats 'just drop the lowercasing at fetchRequestAdapter.ts:531' (leaves T4's canonical writer and non-canonical caller spellings leaking, and changes the header contract relied on by retryHandler.ts:84).
